sets.title: My own key word transformation set

questions.first: If you don't leave now, you will miss the train.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' introduces the one condition under which the result will NOT happen, so it replaces the negative if-clause.

questions.first: Someone stole my bicycle outside the station yesterday.
questions.explanation: The focus moves from the unknown thief to the bicycle, so the passive voice is needed.

questions.first: "I will finish the report by Friday," said Theo.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'will' in the original statement becomes 'would'.

questions.first: It is possible that Mia is still at work.
questions.explanation: 'Might be' expresses the same degree of possibility as 'it is possible that ... is'.

questions.first: This museum is less interesting than the one we visited last year.
questions.after: the one we visited last year.
questions.explanation: 'Less interesting than' can be rephrased as a negative equal comparison: 'not as interesting as'.

questions.first: The scientist who won the award studies ocean currents.
questions.explanation: A relative clause with 'who' identifies which scientist is meant.
